prompt: A state government wants to raise its high school graduation rate from 78% to 85%. The candidate's framework: (1) School-level factors: teacher quality and class sizes; (2) Student-level factors: attendance and academic performance; (3) Programs the state already funds. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 1 and 2 overlap: attendance depends on teacher quality
options.feedback: Teachers can affect attendance, but school factors and student factors are different units of analysis.

options.text: Bucket 1 doesn't belong: dropping out is a student's choice
options.feedback: Teaching quality and class sizes affect whether students stay in school. Bucket 1 belongs.

options.text: Missing: family income, health and other factors outside school
options.feedback: Right. Out-of-school factors drive many dropouts, and neither the school nor the student bucket covers them.

options.text: It's a generic education framework: it isn't split by school district
options.feedback: District can be a cut inside each bucket. The flaw is the missing out-of-school factors.

explanation: Dropouts come from school, student and out-of-school factors. The third group, plus the programs available to act on each, is missing.

extras.corrected_framework: School factors; student factors; out-of-school factors; available programs and their cost
